song.title: Where The Streets Have No Name

guitar.evidence: The Edge's Gibson Explorer (used on 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and others) and Stratocaster/Rickenbacker use are extremely well documented, alongside his effects-driven sound.
guitar.notes: Original entry already correct; refined model list with Rickenbacker (used heavily on early albums) replacing Gretsch.

tone.target: shimmering delay-soaked Vox clean with chime
tone.profile: shimmering delay-soaked Vox clean with chime
tone.summary: Clean signal chain utilizing light compression and a Vox-style amp/cab combination, heavily augmented by Digital Delay for shimmering arpeggios.

rig.name: U2 - Where The Streets Have No Name - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide smooth sustain and even out dynamics for arpeggios.
Keep the tone clean and transparent; avoid thick distortion.
Simulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30.
Provide a classic British clean tone foundation.
blocks.gap: The AC30 is often paired with specific cabinet models; UK Vintage 4x12 provides the necessary clarity and bite.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the bright arpeggios and add clarity to the high end.
Keep the tone open and avoid unnecessary filtering.
Create the core shimmering effect and dotted-eighth delay required.
Add subtle shimmer and space without the 'big hall wash'.
blocks.gap: Avoided large reverb, but Plate offers a controlled, shimmering tail.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better match the Vox AC30's natural pairing, enhancing the bright, shimmering clean tone.

proposals.reason: Better matches the AC30 amp model for optimal chime and clarity.
